speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in; I see you have chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination. To better understand your symptoms, how long have you been experiencing these issues, and do you notice any pain specifically when you urinate?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the fact that your discomfort improves after voiding is significant. Given your age, the 5-month duration, and recent painful intercourse, do you notice any burning, fever, or visible blood in your urine? Also, have you been diagnosed with Interstitial Cystitis or BPH previously?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome. The combination of chronic bladder pain relieved by voiding, significant urinary frequency, and dyspareunia in a middle-aged woman is classic for this condition.
